title: UNDERTHRONE: a 3D fighting game built in 3 days with Meshy, Mixamo, Claude and Godot. Here's the full AI pipeline.
author: Siniestrorr
selftext:
Solo dev from Guayaquil, Ecuador. I wanted to see how far generative AI could push a small team of one, so I built a 3D street fighting game with 10 characters in about 3 days. Here is exactly how the pipeline worked.

1. Characters (Meshy)\*\*

All 10 fighters were generated in Meshy from text and image prompts. The raw meshes were cleaned and decimated with Blender Python scripts before rigging.



\*\*2. Rigging and animation (Mixamo)\*\*

Auto-rigged in Mixamo, with around 13 fight animations per character (strikes, kicks, specials, supers, hit reactions, knockdowns).



\*\*3. Technical pipeline (Claude + Blender Python)\*\*

This was the hardest part, and where Claude did the heavy lifting. It wrote scripts that:

\- retarget every animation with a world-space pose copy plus arm IK, fixing the collapsed elbows and shoulders Mixamo often produces

\- transfer skin weights from the rigged low-poly onto the original high-res Meshy mesh, protecting the hands and face

\- export everything to Godot in HD with 60 fps animation and proper texture and normal-map import settings



\*\*4. Gameplay (Godot 4 + Claude)\*\*

Fighting engine written in GDScript with Claude: frame data with startup, active and recovery frames per move, hitboxes driven by bone positions, cancel chains, juggles, command inputs (quarter-circle and dragon punch), cinematic supers, CPU AI, rounds, menus and character select.



\*\*5. Trailer\*\*

Every shot was recorded in-engine with Godot's Movie Maker using scripted cameras: first-person, orbit, low-angle and bullet-time freezes. Claude then edited it to the beat of my original track with a Python and ffmpeg editor.



\*\*Takeaway\*\*

AI didn't replace the design work. Direction, the feel of each fight, testing and the music were mine. But it removed weeks of technical grind, especially retargeting and engine code.
